Chapter 9: Leadership and Influence—Setting the Relentless Standard.
You know, being relentless isn't just about pushing yourself—it's about lifting up everyone around you. Whether it’s in business, on the field, or even at home, someone who lives relentlessly sets the bar for the whole group.
Here’s the thing—leadership in this sense doesn’t come from a title or an official position. It’s about showing, not telling. The relentless leader sets the tone by what they do: showing up early, putting in the tough hours, and sticking to the highest standards, even when no one’s watching.
Influence? It just happens naturally when you lead like this. People aren’t moved by fancy speeches—they’re moved by watching someone show integrity and consistency, day after day. It’s a quiet kind of leadership, but wow, does it change the culture. Suddenly, excuses disappear, and accountability becomes the expectation.
So, what does it actually look like to lead relentlessly? Let’s break it down:
First, model the standards you expect from everyone else. Even if you’re the only one in the room—especially then.
Next, don’t shy away from honest, direct feedback. It’s not about being harsh—it’s about helping others grow and improve.
Support your team through tough times, but don’t ever drop the bar for excellence. People rise to the expectations you set.
And don’t forget to celebrate the effort and the progress, not just the big wins. Sometimes, improvement is the real victory.
Finally, create an environment where mistakes aren’t something to hide—they’re chances to learn. When people know it’s safe to stumble and get back up, they’ll take the risks that lead to real growth.
Relentless leaders might not always win the popularity contest, but they earn deep respect. Why? Because they challenge others to reach their potential, and they make the tough calls when the team needs it. Their influence lasts, precisely because it’s rooted in authenticity and a rock-solid commitment.
Picture a manager who stays late to help a team member who’s struggling, or a coach who pushes players to be their best—but is right there supporting them through every setback. That’s what relentless leadership is all about. It’s demanding, sure, but it’s also compassionate. Because true greatness? It always needs both.
